autoSwap.enabledDescription: Also switch the account new sessions start on, using the same limits.
autoSwap.sessionThresholdDescription: Swap away once the 5-hour window reaches this. 90% matches claude-swap.
autoSwap.weeklyThresholdDescription: Swap away once the weekly (or a per-model weekly) window reaches this.
autoSwap.hysteresisDescription: A swap target needs this many more points of headroom than the current account, and must be under its own limits, so swaps never bounce.
autoSwap.cooldownDescription: Minimum time between swaps before a limit. A full window or dead login skips it.
autoSwap.failoverDescription: Swap immediately when the current login expires or is revoked, and pause that account.
autoSwap.modelLimitsDescription: Treat a model-specific weekly cap like the weekly limit.
autoSwap.apiKeyFallbackDescription: Launch on a pay-as-you-go key when every subscription is exhausted.
autoSwap.liveSessionsDescription: Seal polls every account’s 5-hour and weekly usage and moves a running agent to another account before it crosses a limit below, or right away if its login dies. It resumes the conversation when it cannot switch live.
autoSwap.rateLimitFallbackDescription: Last resort only. If an agent stops with a usage-limit message that polling has not caught yet, move it anyway.
autoSwap.title: Auto-swap
autoSwap.description: Seal reads every account’s 5-hour and 7-day usage and moves work to the next account in the list before a limit is hit. Each provider has its own settings.

onboarding.title: Add your first account
onboarding.body: Seal runs Claude Code and Codex on the accounts you add here. With two or more, it watches each account’s 5-hour and 7-day usage and moves work to the next one before a limit stops you.
onboarding.step1: Add each subscription. Every sign-in gets a folder of its own, so accounts never overwrite each other.
onboarding.step2: Drag accounts into the order you prefer, and turn on auto-swap.
onboarding.step3: Optionally pin projects or machines to specific accounts with rules, and push logins to your other machines.
